Name: Mbed TLS as a vendor static archive, Cortex-M3
Why: The shape case 001 only exercised by analogy. A vendor SDK ships libmbedcrypto.a carrying 86 object files; this firmware needs three of them. Nothing in the source tree, the build files or the archive itself says which three -- only the link does. It also fixes everything case 001 could not establish: the commit is recorded, the artifact is hashed, the version is read from the built header and the licence from the SPDX identifiers of the members that shipped.

Target.Board: none -- a link target, not a runnable image

Toolchain.ContainerNote: libnewlib-arm-none-eabi is a SEPARATE Debian package. gcc-arm-none-eabi alone gives a compiler with no libc headers and the build fails on `string.h: No such file or directory`. The Dockerfile in this directory has the full list.
Toolchain.ConfigNote: A deliberately minimal MBEDTLS_CONFIG_FILE (baremetal_config.h) enabling only AES, SHA-256 and their dependencies. The build still compiles every enabled module into the archive; the image needs three. That gap is the measurement.

Evidence.TotalsNote: CORRECTED 2026-10-13. These figures were re-established after a defect was found in BOTH map readers -- cres_t4.service.linker_map and the Go collector's internal/linkermap. Every sized line in the memory map was being counted, including the output sections an ELF file carries and a device does not run: .debug_*, .comment, .ARM.attributes, .riscv.attributes. Those are stripped before the image is flashed, so counting them inflated every figure by a factor that depends on nothing but the compiler's -g setting. The previous totals are kept in PreviousTotals so the size of the error stays on the record, and the bytes are now reported separately as MetadataBytes rather than dropped.

Reproducibility.Note: Built twice in a fresh container; both the artifact digest and the map bytes were identical. THE TWO-STEP COMPILE-THEN-LINK IS WHY. Doing both in one gcc invocation leaves the app's object as a compiler temporary -- /tmp/ccM19uij.o -- whose name differs on every run, so two equivalent builds produce different maps and reproducibility could never pass. A corpus case has to be reproducible before it can measure anything.

NotScoreable.newlib-version: newlib's own version is not in the archive paths -- only GCC's is -- and the toolchain package manifest was not captured.
